newsitem.title: ROMANIA: ROMANIAN NET GOVERNMENT CREDITS 31 PCT UP IN SEPT.
newsitem.headline: ROMANIAN NET GOVERNMENT CREDITS 31 PCT UP IN SEPT.

text.p: Net credits to Romania's government soared by 31 percent to 2.7 trillion lei in September pushing total domestic loans up by 5.5 percent from August, central bank data (BNR) showed on Friday.
Net loans to government accounted for some 11 percent of domestic credits in September which stood at 24.9 trillion lei.
Over the past few months, the Finance Ministry, keen to cover a bulging state budget deficit, has launched several issues of three-month treasury bills.
The eight-month state budget posted a deficit of 1.9 trillion lei but is envisaged to climb to 4.2 trillion by the end of 1996. Data on the nine-month budget was not available.

The non-government credits went up by 3.0 percent to 22.2 trillion lei at end-September, with loans in hard currency continuing an upward path and expanding by 4.1 percent to 7.6 trillion lei, BNR data showed.
Medium- and long-term loans accounted for 15 percent of end-September leu loans, which amounted to 14.57 trillion lei, up from 14.23 trillion in August.
State companies held 57 percent of end-September leu loans, down from August's 57.6 percent level.
Inflation was 2.4 percent in September, with the year-on-year rate at 45.3 percent.
